69.t: Duke arranged every tune; naming Caravan and Conga Brava
69.s: Duke arranged and recorded everything Tizol wrote; he left titles to Duke or Mills and wrote Conga Brava on request during the conga craze.
69.ch: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
69.q: Everything that I did, Duke arranged. All my tunes. I got quite a few tunes; I don't know if you know them all by their names, but I did quite a few tunes. I don't get too much -- a dollar, three dollars, four dollars, ten dollars -- but I get some all the time. Like Meditation, "Lost in…

69.t: Where and how Caravan was written
69.s: Rose recalls Caravan was written in Los Angeles at the Laveda; Tizol is unsure but remembers playing it for Duke and Mills until Mills liked it.
69.ch: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
69.q: I don't remember where I wrote it -- whether it was in Los Angeles or New York, when I was with Duke, or what. I know that I wrote the tune, and me and Duke used to play it to Irving Mills, to everybody. We'd sit down and Duke would say, 'Let's get the trombone and play Caravan.' And 'Let's see if…

69.s: He wrote it in Chicago, played it for Duke, and Duke arranged and recorded it.
69.ch: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
69.q: I wrote that in Chicago, I think it was. I gave it to Duke to play, and I played it with him -- everything he wanted me to play on the trombone, you know, to see what it sounded like, and then he takes it and made an

69.s: Tizol wrote Conga Brava alone and Duke arranged and recorded it.
69.q: Well, that's one of those things, you know? I wrote it myself. But he did the arrangement and recorded it.

69.s: Mills's name appears for the lyrics but Tizol wrote the music alone with Duke arranging; he doesn't remember Charlie Barnet on maracas.
69.q: Well, I don't know who wrote the lyrics on that one, which I imagine, I guess, Mills getting the credit for that. That's the reason why they put Mills on there, but the music, I only did it myself.

69.t: How Moonlite Fiesta began in Chicago
69.s: He played it on trombone at the Grand Terrace with Duke accompanying, and Duke then arranged it.
69.q: Well, I played it myself on the trombone at the house in Chicago. In Chicago, we were at the Cabaret where Earl Hines used to be for years.

69.s: Credits vary for Pyramid; he wrote it noodling on trombone and Duke arranged it.
69.q: Anything having to do with lyrics, Mills is gonna get on there. But who did it, I don't know. Mills had plenty of publishers to do the things. I guess he gave them some money and they would put his name on them.

69.s: One of his first tunes after Caravan and Perdido, recorded in 1930 on Brunswick without Ellington's name.
69.q: outside of "Caravan" and "Perdido" -- "Admiration," I wrote that later on.

69.s: Cootie played the lead on Jubilesta; he knows nothing of Stevedore Serenade.
69.q: "Jubilesta, Jubilesta." That was a nice tune that Cootie recorded. Cootie played the lead chorus on "Jubilesta" in the recording. Just like I said, Duke would just make the arrangements and we would record them.

106.t: Playing Cole Porter's 'Night and Day' first
106.s: Briggs claims the band was the first to play Porter's 'Night and Day,' which Porter brought in with scores and tested by sitting in at piano.
106.q: And we -- Bricktop had taken Paris by storm, after the tavern she opened, for the simple reason, because we didn't go back to Florence's -- we should have started at Florence's before, but we go back to Florence's after Bricktop.

115.s: He composed the tune at a piano at Chicago's Music Box and people assumed Ellington wrote it.
115.ch: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
115.q: I was sitting at the piano at the Bandbox -- the Music Box, I believe it was, in Chicago. That was right under the Brass Rail.
